subject: [D-RUG]: Do you have a fast computer?

messages.author: e5454a2faff3d470
messages.subject: [D-RUG]: Do you have a fast computer?
parts:
Hey All,
I have a non-parametric repeated measures MANOVA that I am running, and it can resample up to 10,000 iterations, but my computer is only powerful enough to run 3000 before it craps out, and its fairly new and good. If anyone has a really souped up system and would be willing to let the analysis run overnight I would be happy to compensate you somehow. I don't live in Davis and would rather not drive to campus just to use a computer lab. My computer has an i5 processor, 2.5 ghz and 8 gigs of RAM, just for reference. Thanks in advance!

Katie

--
Katherine Smith

I don't know what the rates are for a beefy computer (but they're
published). If you really need only to run this job one time, it
might be worth spending the bucks to rent the computer from Amazon.

-- Mike

messages.author: 452569198af8caee
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Do you have a fast computer?
parts:
The iPlant collaborative, now renamed Cyferse it seems (http://www.cyverse.org/) offers the possibility to create virtual machines up to 16 cores and 128 Gb RAM through their Atmosphere environment, http://www.cyverse.org/atmosphere (and they have many other services). It’s NSA funded (last I heard) and is free for university users. I used it to run simulation and to do beefy image analysis. You need to request access first. They offered a workshop a few years ago in Davis and might offer one in the future (others on this list might know).

But, what do you mean by « craps out »? Is it running out of RAM? Maybe just code optimization might help to free up your computer.

HTH,

Guillaume

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Do you have a fast computer?
parts:
Katie,

I assume your advisor is in the College of Ag & Env Sci. If so, you have
access to the FARM compute cluster.
https://wiki.cse.ucdavis.edu/support/systems/farm

No need to write any fancy code, you can just run a single job, and
easily get 4 Xeon cores, 32 GB RAM (It's actually possible to get up to
8 cores, 64 GB ram on a regular node). There is a little learning curve
to get started though.

Do you get an error message when your code quits?

Enjoy,
Alex Mandel, PhD

Center for Spatial Sciences
http://spatial.ucdavis.edu
Geospatial and Farming Systems Research Consortium
http://gfc.ucdavis.edu
University of California, Davis

messages.author: e5454a2faff3d470
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Do you have a fast computer?
parts:
Hello All!
Thanks for the input. Noam is going to run the code for me. To answer some questions, I don't get an error message. RStudio just freezes up and I have to force close it. No code optimization is possible. I am running a single function. The fact that I can specify how many CPUs I am running within the function should have been the first clue that I would need more power, probably.

require(MANOVA.RM)

RM.model <- RM(TIME ~ WETLAND * PYEAR * NSEASON * FOOD, data = set.time,
             subject = "MOUSEID", no.subf = 1, iter = 10000,
             resampling = "Perm", CPU = 1, seed = 18, dec = 2) 

But I am going to be running some spatial analyses for a later chapter so all of your suggestions will come in handy then!  Thanks!

Katie

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Do you have a fast computer?
parts:
As a note on that. I have found that running scripts with Rscript on
command line is more stable for large analysis than in Rstudio, even on
a very big machine. More likely to crash with a message too, rather than
hang, since the error does not need to get passed back to Rstudio. I'm
guessing your R session crashed in a way that didn't report back to Rstudio.

Enjoy,

Alex Mandel, PhD

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Do you have a fast computer?
parts: From personal use and helping students, I have found 90% of crashes in Rstudio are because of Rstudio. R is pretty difficult to crash outright. I can count on one hand the times I have completely crashed R running through Emacs, and half of those were definitely my fault. Rstudio seems to crash all the time.
